category_title: Highly verbal preschoolers who talk out of turn during group activities
student_description: Sybil is a highly verbal preschooler who enthusiastically dominates conversations and frequently talks over peers, particularly during large group activities like circle time. While she has excellent language skills, she uniquely requires proactive visual cues before activities and explicit, immediate positive reinforcement for practicing physical turn-taking behaviors like raising her hand.

criteria.rationale: Because Sybil struggles with impulse control in the moment, it is essential to establish expectations using visual aids before group activities begin.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include the use of visual supports (e.g., picture cards, visual rules) presented prior to activities to remind Sybil of turn-taking expectations.

criteria.rationale: Because Sybil lacks the foundational understanding of conversational pacing, she needs dedicated time to practice listening and sharing outside of high-stimulation environments.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate explicit teaching methods—such as modeling, role-playing, or direct instruction—focused specifically on practicing social-emotional behaviors like listening and waiting.
